description: Follow-up / query-rewrite eval for MED-264 project RAG. Reuses source_ref values from project_rag_eval_dataset.json (2.1.0); this file does not redefine sources. Questions are conversational follow-ups scored under three retrieval arms (A/B/C). v1.1 multi-turn smoke (2–3 turns). v1.2 adds beyond-default-window rows (4–5 prior turns; default RAG_QUERY_REWRITE_HISTORY_TURNS=3) and more multi-source follow-ups. Still a smoke / first baseline, not a broad reliability proof.

source_corpus.note: Harness must seed/index that corpus, then resolve expected_sources[].source_ref against it. Do not copy sources into this file.

A.purpose: Baseline without rewrite: how well does the raw short follow-up retrieve?

B.purpose: Upper-bound reference only: if the question were completed correctly by a human, how much can retrieval improve? B must not be reported as proof that rewrite_project_question works.

C.purpose: Real rewrite path. Timeouts and other fallbacks that return the original question still count toward C's score.

scoring_notes: Rank each arm with the same evidence-aware single-source / multi-source rules as the main project RAG eval (expected_sources + evidence spans). Do not merge follow-up results into the 2.1.0 Hit@K / MRR aggregates. expected_rewrite is a human reference for arm B and for qualitative review of C; C need not match it verbatim if meaning and referents are preserved. For already_complete and topic_shift, expected_rewrite is intentionally close to question so A and B should be similar and C must not regress by grafting prior turns. For underspecified, prior turns leave multiple plausible referents — expected_rewrite must not pick one. question_type no-answer means the answer should abstain (empty expected_sources); it does not forbid resolving a unique referent in expected_rewrite (see fq20). Rows tagged multi-turn have 2+ completed prior turns; rewrite must bind anaphors to the most recent clear referent and must not graft an older turn after a topic shift. Tag beyond-default-window means history_turn_count > default RAG_QUERY_REWRITE_HISTORY_TURNS (3): the oldest turn(s) are dropped from the rewrite prompt — C must not invent facts that appear only outside the window. Multi-source follow-ups use the same Recall/Full-Coverage scorers as the main eval. Reports must list A→C improve/regress, rewrite latency/fallbacks, and call out multi-turn and beyond-default-window subsets.

case_kind_notes.anaphoric: Follow-up needs prior turns to resolve references (e.g. that / she / why was that).
case_kind_notes.already_complete: Current question is already self-contained; rewrite should leave it alone or nearly so, and retrieval must not regress.
case_kind_notes.topic_shift: Current question changes topic; rewrite must not wrongly graft the previous turn.
case_kind_notes.underspecified: Prior turns do not clearly identify the referent; rewrite must not invent facts.

question_fields.question_type: single-source | multi-source | no-answer — same meaning as the main fixture; drives which scorer arm results use.
question_fields.include_in_followup_metrics: true for questions that feed the follow-up aggregate; false for diagnostic-only rows if any.
question_fields.history: Completed prior turns only (not the current question). Each item: {role: user|assistant, content: string}. Oldest first.
question_fields.question: Current user follow-up text (arm A query; also the input to rewrite_project_question for arm C).
question_fields.expected_rewrite: Human-written standalone question for arm B. Reference only; not a verbatim target for C.
question_fields.expected_sources: Same shape as project_rag_eval_dataset.json: [{source_type, source_ref, evidence: [span, ...]}]. source_ref must exist in the source corpus.
question_fields.tags: Optional free-form tags for filtering in reports.
question_fields.notes: Optional author notes about intent or known traps.
question_fields.derived_from: Optional id of the main-fixture question this follow-up was adapted from.
